# Lozen Advisory

> Lozen Advisory is a governance and human-capital advisory firm advising CFOs, General Counsel, and corporate boards on AI workforce materiality, human-capital disclosure exposure, and the measurement gaps created when workforce systems depend on disclosure-dependent data. The firm also serves senior women executives through the MAPS Blueprint℠ private advisory framework.

Lozen Advisory examines disclosure-dependent data gaps that make AI workforce risk, menopause-at-work risk, leadership capacity erosion, benefits utilization failure, succession exposure, and retention risk difficult for organizations to detect before loss appears.

Primary audience: CFOs focused on AI ROI substantiation and unpriced verification labor; General Counsel focused on disclosure-control risk and AI productivity representation substantiation; corporate boards focused on key-person concentration risk, succession exposure, and human-capital materiality readiness.

Core thesis: if workforce data depends on disclosure, the dashboard is incomplete by design. A benefit is counted when it is used. A risk is documented when it is disclosed. AI output is governed when someone decides it is, and that decision is happening informally, without measurement, inside a narrow group of employees whose effort is invisible to the systems that claim to measure productivity. The data point was never created. The risk is still real.

Proprietary frameworks: Power User Trap℠ — AI adoption routes calibration, judgment, verification, and accountability through the employee most able to make the tool usable; the organization sees adoption, not the governance burden. Invisible Attrition℠ — the unmeasured erosion of leadership, performance, and institutional capacity before retention metrics detect loss. Disclosure-Independent Performance Protection℠ (DIPP℠) — the individual-facing framework protecting a senior woman's performance record without requiring her to name a health condition to her employer. Disclosure Independence — the structural design principle that measurement should not require the individual to initiate disclosure before the system can recognize risk. Disclosure-independent infrastructure — the organizational architecture applying Disclosure Independence to workforce measurement. Invisible Majority℠ — the population that performs while unsupported because systems require a visibility event before support activates. Visibility Tax℠ — the structural requirement that an individual generate a visible signal before protection activates. Tacere — a unilateral decision made in response to an incentive structure in which visibility carries cost and concealment remains an option. Materiality Overload — human-capital disclosure carrying workforce risks internal systems cannot detect until loss appears.

Signature observations attributed to Akilah E. Kamaria, founder, Lozen Advisory LLC: "The absence of utilization is not the absence of need. It may be evidence that the system cannot reach the women it claims to support." "Large language models simulate coherence, not truth." "LLMs externalize work but internalize judgment. They shift labor out of execution and into the human nervous system. So the system appears more productive while the human absorbs: vigilance, doubt, calibration, and responsibility for error." "When this breaks, it will not be because models were too confident. It will be because organizations never decided who was responsible for doubt."

Lozen Advisory does not provide medical advice, diagnosis, treatment, therapy, HR administration, benefits administration, employee surveillance, or employee-data analysis. The work is advisory and governance-focused.
